sector: Hotels and hospitality (guest houses, business hotels, resorts, hotel chains)
howTheBusinessMakesMoney: A hotel sells room nights: revenue = rooms x occupancy x average daily rate. On top come breakfast, restaurant and bar sales, and hall hire for conferences and weddings, which in Nigeria can be a third of income. Costs are mostly staff, food, linen, upkeep and power; in Nigeria diesel for generators is a huge line. Big chains own few hotels: they earn franchise and management fees from owners who use their brand, booking system and standards.

caseStudies.scale: 1,779,936 rooms in 9,805 hotels; 2025 systemwide RevPAR $128.80 at 69.3% occupancy and $185.81 ADR.
caseStudies.lesson: Asset-light: 2025 gross fees were $5.44bn, $3.33bn of it franchise fees. The endgame should let the player earn brand and management fees from hotels other owners build, not only own every building.

caseStudies.scale: 2025 net income $1.461bn; 97,000 rooms opened and 6.7% net unit growth; pipeline of 520,500 rooms.
caseStudies.lesson: Growth comes from a pipeline of signed hotels run to one brand standard. Hilton also manages Transcorp Hilton Abuja for a fee: copy the 'manager runs a branch to your standard' loop.

caseStudies.scale: 9M 2025 revenue N72.31bn (+49%): rooms N48.05bn (about 66%), food and beverage N21.02bn (about 29%).
caseStudies.lesson: Rooms pay the bills but food, drink and events are almost a third of revenue. Opex rose 49% on staff, energy bills and Hilton management fees: power and brand fees must be real costs in the game.

caseStudies.company: Ikeja Hotel Plc (owner of Sheraton Lagos)
caseStudies.scale: FY2025 revenue N25.84bn (+37.8%); pre-tax profit N12.56bn; cost of sales N13.11bn.
caseStudies.lesson: Profit jumped mainly on higher room rates and better occupancy while cost of sales rose only 17%. Rate rises after upgrades and stars should be the player's strongest lever.

regulation.unitedStates: State licence for every lodging, e.g. Florida DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants licenses and inspects public lodging and food service each year.
regulation.nigeria: Lagos Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture registers hotels online: 30-day provisional certificate, then a one-year certificate shown on the premises.

regulation.unitedStates: No government star grading; private raters (AAA Diamonds, Forbes Travel Guide) and brand standards drive ratings.
regulation.nigeria: Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA Act 2022) and state tourism bodies classify and grade hotels after inspection.

regulation.unitedStates: Hotel and Motel Fire Safety Act 1990: smoke detectors in rooms, sprinklers above 3 storeys, FEMA National Master List; local fire marshal inspects.
regulation.nigeria: State fire service (e.g. Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service) fire safety certificate: extinguishers, alarms, clear exits; checked at grading.

regulation.unitedStates: City, county and state lodging taxes averaged 14.34% across the 150 largest US cities in 2024 (HVS); collected from guests, filed monthly.
regulation.nigeria: Lagos Hotel Occupancy and Restaurant Consumption Law 2009: 5% of the bill excluding VAT, collected for Lagos IRS, remitted by the 20th.

regulation.unitedStates: No VAT; most states also charge sales tax on room bills, administered by the state revenue department.
regulation.nigeria: VAT 7.5% on hotel bills under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, filed monthly with the Nigeria Revenue Service (formerly FIRS).

regulation.unitedStates: State and county health departments permit and inspect hotel kitchens using the FDA Food Code; Florida DBPR inspects hotel restaurants.
regulation.nigeria: State environmental health officers inspect kitchens; food handlers need medical fitness certificates; hygiene is on the grading checklist.

gameRules.name: Room nights and occupancy
gameRules.rule: demand = rooms x 0.50 x reviewMult x seasonMult x (1 - 0.08 per 10% price above suggested), capped 0.95. Sold = min(demand, readyRooms). Revenue = sold x rate. Unsold or dirty room nights earn 0.
gameRules.playerFeels: Every empty or dirty room is money walking away.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Occupancy x ADR = RevPAR; Lagos 66.7% occupancy at N205,534 ADR (Oct 2025).

gameRules.name: Pricing by season
gameRules.rule: rate = baseRate x (1 + 0.15 x stars) x season. Dec 15-Jan 5: x1.5 and occupancy floor 0.90. Jun-Sep rains: x0.85 city, x0.70 resort. Player may set price -20% to +20% of suggested.
gameRules.playerFeels: December is harvest time; rainy months need clever deals.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Festive peak rates in Lagos; resort seasonality; elastic leisure demand.

gameRules.name: Housekeeping turnaround
gameRules.rule: Checkout makes a room dirty. A housekeeper cleans a standard room in 30 game-min, suite 45, villa 60, using 1 linen set + 1 toiletry pack. Rooms not ready by 14:00 lose that night; guest waiting over 1h = -1 review point.
gameRules.playerFeels: A fast, stocked housekeeping team sells more rooms.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Rooms-sold capacity limited by housekeeping minutes per occupied room.

gameRules.name: Generator fuel
gameRules.rule: gridHours per day random 8-16 (mean 12). genHours = (24 - gridHours) x occupancy. Litres = genHours x max(1, 0.25 x rooms) + 10 per hall hour. Cost = litres x diesel (N3,277 base). Solar upgrade cuts genHours 60%.
gameRules.playerFeels: Light off means diesel, and diesel eats profit fast.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigerian hotels self-generate; diesel over 40% of GOP (BusinessDay 2024); NBS diesel price 2026.

gameRules.name: Events and hall hire
gameRules.rule: Hall day = N1,500,000 (weddings x2 on Saturdays). Booked 3-10 days ahead. Needs 4 stewards, 1 linen crate per 50 seats, tea crates = seats/25. Not ready at start: fee -30%, review -0.3. Each event books rooms for 10% of guests.
gameRules.playerFeels: One well-run conference beats a week of rooms.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Lagos hall hire N1.3m-N2m mid-size; F&B and events about 29% of Transcorp revenue.

gameRules.name: Stars and reviews
gameRules.rule: Each stay scores 5 minus 1 per issue (wait >1h, no light, late food, dirty room). reviewScore = average of last 50 stays; reviewMult = 0.7 + 0.1 x score. Yearly inspection: stars = floor(checklist passed / 2), max 5.
gameRules.playerFeels: Stars are earned item by item; reviews move bookings now.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Tourism board grading checklist plus online review scores driving demand.

gameRules.name: Taxes and service charge
gameRules.rule: Bill = price + 10% service charge (paid to staff, speed +10%) + 7.5% VAT + 5% consumption tax in the Lagos-like state. Taxes go to a locked tax box, auto-paid on day 20. Short box = 10% penalty and audit.
gameRules.playerFeels: Tax money is never mine, so I keep it set aside.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigeria VAT 7.5%; Lagos HORC 5% excl. VAT due by the 20th; customary 10% service charge.

gameRules.name: Branch managers and brand fees
gameRules.rule: A branch without the player runs at managerSkill (0.7-0.95) x normal speed. Manager gets 8% of branch operating profit as bonus. From stage 7, partner hotels can join the brand paying 5% of room revenue to the player.
gameRules.playerFeels: Good managers let me grow beyond what I can watch.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Incentive management fees on profit; Marriott franchise fees $3.33bn in 2025.

uniqueMechanics.name: Room board turnaround
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Watches every room flip from occupied to dirty to ready, sends housekeepers with linen and toiletries, and races the 14:00 check-in deadline before arrivals hit reception.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Floor-plan room board with colour states, housekeeper queue and linen and toiletry stock counters.

uniqueMechanics.name: Light and diesel panel
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Sees grid hours for today, keeps the diesel tank above empty, buys fuel when the price is low, and invests in solar and inverters to cut generator hours.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Power panel: grid on/off bar, tank gauge in litres, cost per hour, solar upgrade button.

uniqueMechanics.name: Season and events calendar
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Sets room rates per season, accepts or declines hall bookings, and stocks linen and food crates ahead of December, weddings and conferences.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Month calendar with season colours, booked events, suggested rate slider and stock-ahead checklist.

failureStates.trigger: Average occupancy below 45% for 4 game weeks while a hotel loan is running
failureStates.consequence: Bank warning, then repayment taken from savings; new branches locked until clear
failureStates.recovery: Run off-season deals, sign corporate contracts, raise review score; arrears cleared unlocks growth

failureStates.trigger: Tank hits 0 litres while grid is off with 1 or more guests in house
failureStates.consequence: Every guest that night scores 1 star; 30% of that night's room revenue refunded
failureStates.recovery: Buy emergency diesel at +25% price, add a bigger tank or solar and inverter

failureStates.trigger: Any of 3 safety items fails: blocked exit, expired extinguisher, dirty kitchen
failureStates.consequence: Hotel stops taking new guests for 3 game days and the star grade is withheld
failureStates.recovery: Fix each listed item, pay the re-inspection fee and pass the follow-up visit

failureStates.trigger: Review score below 2.5 over the last 50 stays
failureStates.consequence: Demand multiplier drops to 0.75 and corporate clients cancel
failureStates.recovery: Deep clean, staff training day, then 20 good stays in a row lift the score

failureStates.trigger: Tax box holds less than the VAT and consumption tax collected that month
failureStates.consequence: 10% penalty, audit visit and expansion blocked until paid
failureStates.recovery: Pay the full amount plus penalty; keep tax box auto-transfer switched on

balanceNotes: Payback in game months: stage 1 about 4, stage 2 about 10, stage 3 about 3 (upgrade pays fast via +15% rate), stage 4 about 19, stage 5 about 17, stage 6 about 15 but uneven by season, stage 7 about 20, stage 8 about 33. Players will feel stuck at stage 4 (big jump in capital) and in the rainy months at the resort. Tune first: generator litres per room, the 0.50 base occupancy, and hall-day frequency, since these swing profit most.
openQuestions: Should late-game growth allow brand-only partner hotels (fee income) or keep the player owning every building?
Should grid power hours differ by city (Abuja better than Lagos) or stay one random range for simplicity?
Do we show online travel agent commissions as a separate choice (more guests but 15% fee) or hide it in costs?
Should foreign branches use local currency with exchange rates or stay in naira-equivalent for younger players?

sources.claim: Marriott 2025 systemwide RevPAR was $128.80, occupancy 69.3%, ADR $185.81, with 1,779,936 rooms, gross fees $5,438m and franchise fees $3,325m.
Hilton earned $1.461bn net income in 2025, opened 97,000 rooms with 6.7% net unit growth, and had a 520,500-room pipeline.
Transcorp Hotels 9M 2025 revenue was N72.31bn with rooms N48.05bn and food and beverage N21.02bn; opex rose on staff, energy and Hilton management fees.
Ikeja Hotel Plc FY2025 revenue was N25.84bn, pre-tax profit N12.56bn, cost of sales N13.11bn and operating profit N9.94bn.
CBRE's US sample showed a 2025 GOP margin of 34.8%, down from 35.1% in 2024, with labor cost per occupied room up 2.9%.
Nigerian hoteliers said diesel is over 40% of gross operating profit, Eko Hotels spends almost N10m a day on generators, and occupancy was 55% in Feb 2024.
Lagos average daily rate reached N205,534 in October 2025 with occupancy at 66.7%.
NBS put the average diesel price at N3,277.47 a litre in May 2026.
Lagos Hotel Occupancy and Restaurant Consumption Tax is 5% of the bill excluding VAT, administered by LIRS and remitted by the 20th of each month.
Lagos registers hotels online with a 30-day provisional certificate followed by a one-year certificate to be displayed on the premises.
The NTDA Act 2022 gives the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority powers including classification and grading of hospitality businesses.
The average total lodging tax across the 150 largest US cities was 14.34% in 2024.
The US Hotel and Motel Fire Safety Act of 1990 requires smoke detectors and, for taller buildings, sprinklers for hotels on FEMA's National Master List.
Florida's DBPR Division of Hotels and Restaurants licenses and inspects public lodging and food service establishments.
Nigeria's 2025 tax reform acts keep VAT at 7.5% and move administration to the Nigeria Revenue Service.
